answer: Each agent must periodically submit a computational proof tied to a mutable on‑ledger saffron seed derived from the previous block’s relic hash, forcing the output to depend on the latest state. The ledger records the proof on a sliding ledge of recent submissions and automatically rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate result, because the unique work requirement cannot be satisfied by cloned identities. An attacker therefore must expend full compute for every fake identity on each round, scaling cost linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
